title: Tunable topological enhancement of covariant quantum Fisher information via non-Bloch skin effect in non-Hermitian SSH lattices
authors: Qi-Cheng Wu, Yan-Hui Zhou, Tong Liu, Dong-Xu Chen, Chui-Ping Yang
abstract: The covariant quantum Fisher information (CQFI) has recently been established as the ultimate precision benchmark for pseudo-Hermitian sensors [Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 080802 (2026)], yet existing analyses are limited to single-mode systems. Here we extend the CQFI formalism to multi-mode non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger lattices and reveal tunable topological enhancement enabled by the non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE). Under open boundary conditions, the NHSE deforms the conventional Brillouin zone into a generalized Brillouin zone of radius r = exp(\k{appa}), where \k{appa} denotes the non-Bloch decay rate. While the total CQFI scales linearly with system size N, its prefactor depends critically on \k{appa}, yielding an enhancement factor E(N) = F_OBC / F_PBC that exceeds 30 for N ~ 30, substantially outperforming periodic-boundary sensors. The enhancement is robust against moderate local disorder and supports multi-parameter estimation, with the joint Cramér-Rao bound reduced by up to 15 orders of magnitude. These findings establish a spatial-domain mechanism for quantum metrology that complements time-domain strategies and is experimentally accessible using topoelectrical circuits, photonic lattices, and superconducting circuits with current technology.
summary: This paper investigates how the non-Hermitian skin effect in SSH lattices can topologically enhance the quantum precision limit, quantified by the CQFI. By comparing open boundary conditions (OBC) to periodic boundary conditions (PBC), the authors show a large, tunable enhancement factor $E(N)$. This establishes a novel, experimentally accessible spatial-domain strategy for quantum metrology.
main_problem: To extend the covariant quantum Fisher information (CQFI) formalism to multi-mode non-Hermitian systems to find a tunable topological enhancement mechanism for quantum metrology.
main_result: The CQFI exhibits a tunable topological enhancement factor $E(N)$ due to the non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE), which can surpass 30 for modest system sizes and significantly reduce estimation uncertainty.
method: The authors calculate the total CQFI by summing contributions over the Generalized Brillouin Zone (GBZ) manifold, utilizing partial-fraction decomposition to find the asymptotic scaling behavior.
model_or_system: The study uses non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) lattices, which are analyzed using a Hamiltonian framework that incorporates non-Hermitian parameters ($\gamma_1, \gamma_2$) leading to the NHSE.
key_observables: Covariant Quantum Fisher Information (CQFI), Enhancement Factor $E(N) = F_{	ext{OBC}}^{	ext{total}} / F_{	ext{PBC}}^{	ext{total}}$, and the joint Cramér-Rao bound.
important_parameters: Non-Bloch decay rate ($\kappa$), system size ($N$), and non-Hermitian asymmetry parameters ($\gamma_1, \gamma_2$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on extending CQFI from single-mode to multi-mode systems and assumes the applicability of non-Bloch band theory for open boundary conditions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the total CQFI scaling (OBC vs. PBC), the enhancement factor $E(N)$ vs. $N$ (showing large enhancement), and the non-monotonic dependence of $E$ on the non-Hermitian parameters $\gamma_1$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the CQFI formalism for non-Hermitian systems, then derives the OBC total CQFI by summing over the GBZ, contrasting this with the PBC sum. The core development involves analyzing the resulting enhancement factor $E(N)$ and demonstrating its tunability and topological origin.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, physically realizable mechanism—the NHSE—to boost quantum sensing precision beyond standard bounds, linking topological properties directly to metrological enhancement in open quantum systems.
